Migration for React consumers (fantasy-draft `lib/useSurface.js` is its own copy and is unaffected until it adopts `@summationai/axe-surface/react`): nothing is required. Handler inputs listed in `deps` only to keep the closure fresh can be dropped. `deps` still carry every value the entry reports (availability, reason, name, value). A mirror outside React that re-applies `attributesFor` on `onChange` should use `subscribe` under an application-owned revision, where `onChange` does not fire on a re-registration.

## Tests

`packages/surface/test/react-mounted.test.ts` (new, `// @vitest-environment jsdom`, 17 tests), `packages/surface/test/surface.test.ts` (one new test), `packages/surface/test/bundle.test.ts` (asserts no jsdom input). Proved with `git stash push -- packages/surface/src`: 9 fail on the original source.

Failing on the original: an id change moves the registration; a target change moves the registration; an act runs the latest render's handler; a field's setter and a collection's more are the latest render's too; an id change under Strict Mode leaves only the new id; an id change is the control's new data-surface-id; the control follows register, unregister, and reconcile made outside the component; subscribes once across re-renders and does not loop (with the original it resubscribed six times to `onChange`; the committed version spies on `subscribe`, which the original lacks); subscribe [S-OBS-4] › fires after every change a reader could see.

Passing on both (no-regression checks for refuted hypotheses): registers on mount, refreshes in place, unregisters on unmount; re-rendering or refreshing one row keeps every row where it was [S-ENT-5]; is safe under Strict Mode (useSurface and useSurfaceProps); freeze and thaw, surface and app mode; availability that returns removes the stale attributes; a live name change; a change in app mode with setRev and no bump.

Bundle: `@summationai/axe-surface` plus `/react` went from 25,290 to 26,308 bytes minified, no Node built-ins, no Zod, no jsdom.

No browser integration was added. jsdom settled every hypothesis. Tearing under concurrent rendering (startTransition with a store change mid-render) is not tested; useSyncExternalStore is React's own guarantee against it, and the snapshot is a string.

## Limitations

- Two mounted components registering the same id on one surface share one row; the first to unmount removes it. The spec now says to give each control its own id. The hook does not reference-count.
- An id or target change registers the new id at the end of the table, like any new id. Its index changes.
- The latest handler is the latest committed render's. A handler invoked during a render that has not committed yet runs the previous one.
- `deps` still govern the data an entry reports. A value left out of `deps` stays stale until something else re-registers the entry. Only functions are always fresh. A `name` given as a function is called at read time, as before.
- The bridge's `onChange` still fires only after `bump`, `freeze`, or `thaw`. Under an application-owned revision (`setRev`, no `bump`), a changed action set is picked up by the next request (the provider is read on every enumeration), but MCP clients get no `tools/list_changed` until a freeze or a bump. That is outside this item (`packages/surface/src/axe.ts` was not touched).
- The mounted tests run under jsdom, not a browser. Layout-before-paint is asserted by React's semantics, not measured.
- `llms.txt` is not updated here (see the report for the wording it needs).

## Status

Done on `review/react`. Verified with `pnpm gen:vocabulary -- --check`, `pnpm -r build`, `pnpm check:snippets`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm -r typecheck`, `pnpm -r test`, and `pnpm docs:api`.


## Follow-up at merge

The limitation above about the bridge is resolved: `surfaceActions(...).onChange` listens on `subscribe` and coalesces to one notification per microtask when `registryVersion` moved. Tests: `packages/surface/test/axe.test.ts` "under an app-owned revision, a row that registers or leaves announces a changed action set with no bump" (fails without the change) and "onChange fires once when the registry changed, coalescing a render's registrations, and not on a bump alone".

# docs/review/2026-09-24/12-limits-and-schema.md

# 12. Resource limits, schema boundaries, retention

Phase 2. Branch `review/limits`, based on `herz/surface-integration` at `ce6ef1d` (phase 1 merged).

Every finding below was reproduced on `ce6ef1d` before any change, with a script against the built packages and then with the regression tests listed under each sub-item. "Fails before" means the test was run with the package's `src/` stashed (`git stash push -- packages/<pkg>/src`) and failed; "guard" means it passed before too and pins behavior the change must keep.

## (a) Retention

### Finding

- `MemoryTokenStore` and `MemoryIdempotencyStore` dropped an expired entry only when that key was read again. Continuation, handoff, and poll tokens an agent abandons, and idempotency keys (unique by design), are never read again: 1000 claims with a 1-second TTL, then a write 10 seconds later, left 1001 entries. `MemoryTokenStore` also read `Date.now` directly, so it could not be tested with a clock.
- `SqliteIdempotencyStore.prune()` existed, undocumented, without a cutoff or an index on `expires`.
- Other in-memory structures, checked: the server's per-request `callers` map is a `WeakMap` keyed by `Request` (released with the request); handoff records live in the `TokenStore` (now bounded); Surface's ledger is already bounded (`ledger.max`, default 1000) and `scopedSurfaces` has `idleMs` and `onEvict`. `@summationai/axe-mcp`'s issued-poll-URL set is bounded to the most recent 1000 (owned by the MCP item; not edited here). `AXE.changeListeners` grows only with the application's own `onActionsChanged` calls, each of which returns an unsubscribe.

### Change

- `packages/core/src/retention.ts` (new): `ExpiringMap`, shared by both memory stores. Options (`RetentionOptions`): `now` (injectable clock), `maxEntries` (default 10000, `DEFAULT_MAX_ENTRIES`), `sweepIntervalMs` (default 60000, `DEFAULT_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS`). A write sweeps expired entries when the interval has passed or the map is full; at `maxEntries` the oldest evictable entries go first. No timer, so nothing keeps a process alive.
- `MemoryIdempotencyStore(options)`: a claim whose lease is running is never evicted (that would let the operation run twice); completed records and claims past their lease are. When every entry is a running claim, `claim` throws rather than evict one. `sweep()` and `close()` (drops everything; later calls throw).
- `MemoryTokenStore(options)`: same options, `sweep()`, `close()`. An evicted token answers `not_found`.
- `SqliteIdempotencyStore.prune(before = now)`: refuses a future cutoff; `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS <table>_expires`; the SQL for a job outside Node is documented.
- Spec [P-LIM-4]. Docs: `docs/deploying.md` "Limits and retention" (with `docs/examples/deploying/limits.ts#memory` and `#prune`), checklist lines.

### Tests

`packages/core/test/limits.test.ts`, all failing before:

- "MemoryTokenStore sweeps expired records on a later write, whether or not they are read again"
- "MemoryTokenStore evicts the oldest record at maxEntries"
- "MemoryIdempotencyStore sweeps abandoned unique keys, and evicts completed entries before a running claim" (also: full of running claims throws; a claim past its lease becomes evictable)
- "sweep() and close(): close drops every entry and later use fails"
- "the stores refuse a maxEntries that is not a positive integer"
- "a server on the default stores keeps a bounded number of tokens for abandoned continuations" (200 abandoned continuations, `maxEntries: 50`, 50 held)
- "SqliteIdempotencyStore.prune ... deletes rows that expired before the given time and keeps live ones; a future time is refused" (skipped where `node:sqlite` is missing; run on Node 24.21)

### Limitations

- A store at `maxEntries` shortens the idempotency window for the evicted keys: a retry of an evicted completed operation runs the handler again. Production multi-instance deployments use a shared store anyway.
- Sweeping happens on writes; an idle process keeps its expired entries until the next write (its memory is not growing).
- `prune()` must be scheduled by the site; the SDK does not start a job.

## (b) Body limits

### Finding

- The core read every body with `request.text()`: a 5 MiB body to a read-only action returned 200 after buffering all of it. There was no limit anywhere in `@summationai/axe-core`.
- A body of 100000 nested arrays (about 200 KB) crashed `handle()` with `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` in canonicalJson (the fingerprint hash), before any schema ran; the adapters turned it into a 500 or an unhandled rejection.
- `@summationai/axe-express` and `@summationai/axe-next` (Pages) read an unread Node stream to its end with no limit before calling the core.
- `@summationai/axe-client` read every response with `res.json()`, unbounded.
- Found by the new conformance checks against the getting-started Express server: behind `express.json()`, a 20000-level body parsed fine and then overflowed `JSON.stringify` in the adapter (HTTP 500); the Next Pages adapter did the same and never answered. And `express.json()` in front refuses a large body with its own HTML 413, which is no AXE envelope.

### Change

- `createAXE({ maxBodyBytes })`, default 1 MiB (`DEFAULT_MAX_BODY_BYTES`), exposed as `axe.maxBodyBytes`; a non-positive or fractional value throws at startup. readBody refuses a `Content-Length` above the limit without reading; otherwise it reads the `Request` stream with a counter and cancels it once past the limit. Refusal: `invalid_input`, `retryable: false`, `details: { reason: "payload_too_large", maxBodyBytes }`, HTTP 413, before JSON parsing, identity, tokens, or hooks. It takes precedence over an unknown action name. Decision: reuse `invalid_input` with a reason rather than add an error code (DECISIONS.md).
- Nesting: a parsed body deeper than 64 levels (`MAX_JSON_DEPTH`) is `invalid_input` with an issue at `""`; the depth check is iterative.
- Express and Next Pages: the raw stream is read only up to `maxBodyBytes + 1` bytes (nothing when `Content-Length` is larger), the core answers 413, and the adapter sets `Connection: close` instead of draining. A body a parser already consumed is bounded by that parser (`express.json()` 100 kB, Next 1 MB), then by `maxBodyBytes` on the re-serialized value. `toWebRequest(req, origin, { maxBodyBytes })`. A parsed body too deep for `JSON.stringify` is replaced by a body nested just past the core's limit, so the core answers `invalid_input` instead of the adapter failing. The getting-started Express example now mounts `axeExpress` before `express.json()`, and `docs/integrations/express.md` recommends that order.
- Client: `maxResponseBytes` (default 4 MiB) enforced from `Content-Length` and while reading, in `send()` (sub-item c).
- Vocabulary: reason `payload_too_large`, field and API `maxBodyBytes`. Spec [P-LIM-1], [P-LIM-2]; [P-INV-6] amended for 413. `spec/KINDS.md` notes the interaction with `document.base64`.
- Conformance: `runtime.body-limit` (streams up to 32 MiB of never-valid JSON, so no handler can run; passes on 413 with the envelope and reason, warns on a 413 without an envelope, which is a proxy or body parser in front) and `runtime.nesting-limit`.

### Tests

- `packages/core/test/limits.test.ts`, all failing before: "a Content-Length above maxBodyBytes is refused with 413 and payload_too_large before anything is read", "a body without Content-Length is read only up to the limit, then the stream is cancelled", "the default limit is 1 MiB: 2 MiB is refused, a body under the limit runs", "continue and resume bodies are bounded too, and an unknown action does not hide the refusal", "createAXE refuses a maxBodyBytes that is not a positive integer", "a deeply nested body is invalid_input, not a crash". Guard: "nesting at the limit is accepted".
- `packages/express/test/express.test.ts`: "a raw body whose Content-Length exceeds the limit is refused with 413 before it is read", "a chunked raw body is read only past the limit, then refused with 413 without waiting for the rest". The client sends headers and the first chunk and never the rest; before the change the adapter waited for the end of the body and both tests timed out.
- `packages/next/test/next.test.ts`: "an unparsed raw body is read only past maxBodyBytes and refused with 413, declared or chunked" (timed out before); "a deeply nested body Next already parsed is invalid_input, not a 500" (timed out before, with a `RangeError` in the handler).
- `packages/express/test/express.test.ts`: "a deeply nested body parsed by express.json() is invalid_input, not a 500 [P-LIM-2]" (500 before).
- `packages/testing/test/conformance.test.ts`: "runtime.body-limit passes by default and fails when the server reads a 32 MiB body in full".
- Updated: `packages/core/test/tokens.test.ts` "enforces the 10 MiB decoded-size limit on document.base64 payloads" now sets `maxBodyBytes: 16 MiB`, since a 10 MiB document is about 14 MiB of base64.

### Limitations

- The default 1 MiB caps inline `document.base64` at about 750 KiB; sites that accept larger ones raise `maxBodyBytes`.
- One limit for every endpoint; there is no per-action limit.
- The adapters close the connection after a 413 on an unread body; a client that pipelines requests on that connection must reconnect.
- The body limit bounds, but does not remove, regular-expression cost (sub-item e).

## (c) Client timeouts, cancellation, polling budgets

### Finding

- No timeout: a site that never answered, or stalled after the headers, hung `invoke` forever.
- `signal` existed on `invoke`/`continue`/`resume`/`poll`/`state` but not on `discover` or `AXEClient.discover`; discovery swallowed every error per candidate, so an abort would have moved on to the next URL.
- `poll()` slept `retryAfter * 1000` ms: a site answering `retryAfter: 0` (or a non-number, giving `NaN`) was polled in a tight loop until `maxWaitMs` (with fake timers, ten seconds of polling made far more than ten requests). There was no attempt limit, and `run()` gave each poll its own `maxWaitMs`, so a ladder with several `pending` rungs could poll for maxSteps × `maxWaitMs`.

### Change

All in `packages/client/src/index.ts`, inside the module `send()` (so the trust checks still run on every hop), `ClientOptions`, `PollOptions`, `DiscoverOptions`, and method signatures; nothing reordered.

- `timeoutMs` (default 30000) per request: one `AbortController` per call, aborted by the caller's signal or an `unref`'d timer that covers every redirect hop and the body read (the returned response's body is wrapped; the timer is cleared when it ends, errors, or is cancelled). A timeout is `AXEClientError` "timed out after N ms"; an abort is "was aborted"; an already-aborted signal sends nothing.
- `signal` on `discover(url, { signal })` and `AXEClient.discover(url, options, { signal })`; an aborted discovery rethrows instead of trying the next candidate. Discovery also takes `timeoutMs` and `maxResponseBytes`, and cancels the body of a candidate it skips.
- `maxResponseBytes` (default 4 MiB): see (b).
- `maxPollAttempts` (default 60) and `maxWaitMs` (default 60000) form one budget; `run()` shares it across every poll of the run, starting at the first poll. Each wait is `retryAfter` clamped to at least 1000 ms and at most what is left of `maxWaitMs`.
- Vocabulary: `timeoutMs`, `maxResponseBytes`, `maxPollAttempts`. Spec [P-LIM-3]. Docs: `docs/for-agent-builders.md` "Timeouts, cancellation, and budgets" with `docs/examples/for-agent-builders/limits.ts`.

### Tests

`packages/client/test/limits.test.ts`, with Vitest fake timers (no sleeps). Failing before: "a request that never answers fails with a timeout after timeoutMs", "a body that stalls after the headers is covered by the same timeout", "the default timeout is 30 seconds, and a finished request leaves no timer behind", "aborting mid-request rejects with an AXEClientError", "an already-aborted signal sends nothing, on invoke, continue, resume, poll, state, run, and discover", "aborting discovery stops it instead of trying the next candidate", "a site that says retryAfter 0 is polled at most once a second, not in a loop", "maxPollAttempts bounds the number of polls, default 60", "run() shares one budget across every poll of the run", and the three "response size" tests (before the change the unbounded read ran the worker out of memory). Guard: "a long retryAfter is clamped to what is left of maxWaitMs".

### Limitations

- The timeout is per request, not per `run()`; a run's total time is bounded by maxSteps, the polling budget, and the per-request timeout together.
- `AXEClientError` has no machine-readable reason field; callers distinguish a timeout from an abort by message or by checking their own signal.
- Retries after `rate_limited`/`unavailable` keep their existing rule (`retries`, `maxRetryAfterMs`).

## (d) Malformed untrusted input on the client

### Finding

isResult checked only that `status` was one of the five values, and looksLikeManifest only `protocol`, `baseUrl`, and that `actions` was an array. Reproduced with a mocked site:

- `{ "status": "needs_input", ... }` without `accepts`: `run()` crashed with a `TypeError` inside `fulfill` (`accepts` is not iterable).
- `ok` without `output`, `error` without `error`, `needs_human` without `handoff.url`, `pending` with `retryAfter: "soon"` (a polling loop, see c), a numeric `error.code`, an object `rev`: all returned to the caller as if valid, reaching the agent loop and `present()`.
- A manifest with `actions: [null]` crashed `client.action(name)`; `policies.agents.deny: "acme"` crashed `allowed()` for a client with a vendor; a live-state document `{ "actions": null }` was returned from `state()`.
- `__proto__` keys: `JSON.parse` makes them own data properties, and the client never merged server objects, so nothing was polluted; but getPointer in `@summationai/axe-core/display` (used by `present`) followed `"/constructor"` and `"/__proto__"` into the prototype chain.

### Change

- `packages/client/src/index.ts`: resultProblem, manifestProblem, liveStateProblem, compact hand checks of own members, per status: `needs_input` requires `reason`, `message`, `continuationToken`, `expiresAt`, and a non-empty `accepts` of `{ kind, title, description, schema, sensitive, instructions? }`; `needs_human` a full handoff; `pending` a string `pollUrl` and a finite `retryAfter`; `error` `{ code, message, retryable, details? }`; `rev` a string or finite number. Manifests: `protocol`, `name`, `description`, `baseUrl`, and each action's `name`, `title`, `description`, `input`, `output`, `readOnly`, with `display`, `affordances`, `live`, and `policies.agents` typed when present. A failure is `AXEClientError` naming the member ("... is not an AXE result envelope: accepts must be a non-empty array"); discovery lists rejected candidates under "Not usable".
- Decision: hand checks rather than `@summationai/axe-core/schemas`, which would pull Zod into the dependency-free client (DECISIONS.md). Bundle: 12.1 kB to 16.0 kB minified with (c) and (d); budget raised from 15 kB to 18 kB in `bundle-size.test.ts`.
- `packages/core/src/pointer.ts`: getPointer and schema stepping follow own members only.
- Huge arrays are bounded by `maxResponseBytes`; deeply nested JSON parses (V8's parser is iterative) and nothing in the client or `present` recurses on it.

### Tests

`packages/client/test/limits.test.ts`, "malformed documents from a site are AXEClientError": the invoke-and-run cases for ok without output, needs_input without accepts, a null accepts entry, needs_human without `handoff.url`, pending with a string `retryAfter`, pending without `pollUrl`, error without error, a numeric code, an object `rev`; "discover() rejects malformed manifests and says why"; "state() rejects a live-state document with the wrong shape" (all failing before). Guards: an array body, an unknown status, a status only through `__proto__`, "__proto__ keys in an output stay data: nothing is polluted and present() works", "a deeply nested output does not crash run() or present()".

### Limitations

- The checks cover the members the client and `present` read, not the whole manifest schema; a manifest with a malformed `display` object inside a valid action is accepted and handled by `resolveDisplay`'s own defensiveness.
- A manifest passed to `new AXEClient` directly is not checked; the caller chose it.

## (e) JSON Schema subset audit

### Finding

Reproduced against `validateJsonSchema` on `ce6ef1d`:

- Prototype chain: `additionalProperties: false` accepted `{"__proto__": 1, "constructor": 2, "toString": 3}` (the `key in props` test found them on `Object.prototype`, and the validator then "validated" against `Object.prototype` itself); `required: ["toString"]` was satisfied by `{}`.
- `{ "$ref": "#" }`, or two `$defs` referring to each other: `RangeError` (stack overflow). `{ "$ref": "#anchor" }` threw from the pointer parser.
- `pattern: "("`: `SyntaxError` thrown out of the validator; on `/axe/continue` it escaped `handle()`.
- `format: "ipv4"` (and any unknown format): silently accepted `"not-an-ip"`.
- `patternProperties`, `propertyNames`, `minProperties`, `if`/`then`/`else`, `uniqueItems`, `contains`, `dependentRequired`, `unevaluatedProperties`, and every other unimplemented keyword: silently ignored, so the value passed.
- `multipleOf` used an absolute tolerance of 1e-9 on the quotient.
- `@summationai/axe-generate`: a `format` replaced the string schema, dropping `minLength`, `maxLength`, and `pattern` (`{ format: "email", maxLength: 20 }` accepted any length); an `additionalProperties` schema beside `properties` became `.loose()` (anything); a pattern that did not compile was dropped silently; unknown formats and unsupported keywords were dropped without a warning.
- `toJsonSchema` (Zod 4's converter with `unrepresentable: "any"`): `.refine`/`.superRefine` are dropped, `z.custom` and `z.date()` become `{}`, and `z.preprocess` publishes the inner schema; the manifest claimed a looser schema than the server enforced, silently.
- Fingerprints: phase 1 hashed the parsed input. With `z.string().transform((s) => new Date(s))`, every input hashed as `{}`: reusing an `idempotencyKey` with a different date returned the first date's result instead of `conflict` ([P-IDEM-3] violated). replayForUnknown hashed the raw input, inconsistent with the rest. A login handoff stored the parsed input and parsed it again at resume, so a transform ran twice (the resume failed with `invalid_input`).

### Change

- `packages/core/src/json-schema.ts`, rewritten: own members only; unknown keywords, array `items`, formats neither checked nor carried by a `pattern` (directly or in an `allOf` member), patterns that do not compile (tried with `u`, then without), non-local and plain-name refs, `$ref` loops that consume nothing (tracked per value location), and recursion past 128 levels are issues, never throws. Implemented: `patternProperties`, `propertyNames`, `minProperties`, `maxProperties`, `dependentRequired`, `dependentSchemas`, `uniqueItems`, `contains`, `minContains`, `maxContains`, `if`/`then`/`else`; formats `ipv4` and `jwt`; exact decimal `multipleOf` (BigInt on the shortest decimal form). Compiled patterns are cached (512). New exports: `SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_KEYWORDS`, compilePattern, `isBacktrackingPattern`, `schemaProblems`, `SchemaProblem`.
- `packages/core/src/zod-json-schema.ts`: for `io: "input"`, a node with a custom check, a custom or unrepresentable type, or a preprocess carries `"x-axe-refined": true` (via Zod's `override` hook). Transforms, defaults, and coercion are not marked (reasons in `docs/schemas.md`).
- `packages/core/src/lint.ts`: lintSchema; rules `unsupported-schema` (error), `backtracking-pattern` (warning), `refined-schema` (warning, input only), run by `lintAction` and so by `axe validate` and `axe audit`. Decision for refinements: mark in the manifest and warn through the lint, not reject at registration (DECISIONS.md).
- ReDoS: `isBacktrackingPattern` flags a group repeated without bound whose body ends in an unbounded repetition with nothing required after it; none of Zod's built-in format patterns trip it. The body limit bounds input length. Documented, not enforced at runtime.
- Fingerprint: `server.ts` hashes `input` as sent (canonical JSON) for the idempotency fingerprint and token binding, and a login handoff stores the raw input. Consistent with replayForUnknown.
- `packages/generate/src/json-schema-to-zod.ts`: length and pattern apply with a format; an `additionalProperties` schema beside `properties` is a `.catchall()`; unchecked formats (except `byte`, `binary`, `password`), bad patterns, and 19 unsupported keywords each produce an `unsupported-schema` warning naming the path.
- Validator dependency: Ajv measured and rejected (DECISIONS.md, `docs/schemas.md`): see the table below.
- Spec §5.4 [P-SCHEMA-1] to [P-SCHEMA-6]; vocabulary section "JSON Schema keywords", field `x-axe-refined`, API `schemaProblems`, `validateJsonSchema`, `lintAction`, `isBacktrackingPattern`. New page `docs/schemas.md` (in `docs/README.md` and `site/build.mjs` HUB_GROUPS), with `docs/examples/schemas/refined.ts`; `docs/requirements-and-kinds.md`, `docs/designing-actions.md` (anti-pattern), `docs/security.md`.
- Incidental: `packages/testing/src/drift.ts` kept unknown names in a plain object, so a docs code span reading `constructor` crashed the drift check (`unknown[name].push is not a function`); it now uses a prototype-less object.

### The supported subset

| Keyword | Validator | Zod to JSON Schema | `@summationai/axe-generate` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type`, `enum`, `const` | checked | emitted | converted (primitive `enum`/`const` only) |
| `properties`, `required`, `additionalProperties` | checked, own members | emitted | converted; schema-valued `additionalProperties` is a record or catchall |
| `patternProperties`, `propertyNames` | checked | `propertyNames` for record keys | warning, dropped |
| `minProperties`, `maxProperties`, `dependentRequired`, `dependentSchemas` | checked | not emitted | warning, dropped |
| `items` (schema), `minItems`, `maxItems` | checked | emitted | converted |
| `prefixItems` | checked | emitted for tuples | warning, dropped |
| `uniqueItems`, `contains`, `minContains`, `maxContains` | checked | not emitted | warning, dropped |
| `minLength`, `maxLength` | checked (code points) | emitted | converted, also with a format |
| `pattern` | ECMAScript; uncompilable refuses | emitted | converted; uncompilable warns |
| `format` | date, date-time, time, duration, email, uri, uuid, ipv4, jwt; others only via a pattern, else refused | emitted with a pattern for most | date-time, date, time, email, uri/url, uuid; others warn |
| numeric bounds, `multipleOf` | checked; `multipleOf` exact on decimals | emitted | converted |
| `allOf`, `anyOf`, `oneOf`, `not` | checked | emitted | `allOf` object merge; `anyOf`/`oneOf` union (exclusivity not enforced); `not` warns |
| `if`, `then`, `else` | checked | not emitted | warning, dropped |
| `$ref`, `$defs` | local only; loops that consume nothing refuse | recursion only | local; recursion becomes unknown with a warning |
| `unevaluated*`, `$dynamicRef`, `dependencies`, `additionalItems`, array `items`, anything else | refuses | never emitted | warning, dropped |
| annotations, `x-` keywords | ignored | `description`, `default`, `x-axe-refined` | `description`, `default` used |

Measured sizes (esbuild, minified, browser, Node 24): `@summationai/axe-core/json-schema` 10072 bytes (3566 gzipped); Ajv 8.20 draft 2020-12 entry 133746 (40273); with `ajv-formats` 148303 (43816). The Surface browser bundle (`@summationai/axe-surface` and `/react`) went from 25290 to 30351 bytes with the new validator, under its 50 kB bound; the client bundle does not include the validator.

### Tests

`packages/core/test/schema-boundaries.test.ts`, all failing before except "a recursive schema still validates a recursive value" (guard): "__proto__, constructor, and toString are ordinary keys: additionalProperties: false refuses them", "a required key is not satisfied by the prototype chain", "a $ref cannot resolve through the prototype chain", "a $ref loop that consumes nothing is an issue, not a stack overflow", "a value nested deeper than the validator follows is an issue, not a stack overflow", "a pattern that does not compile refuses the value instead of throwing", "a format the validator cannot check refuses the value unless a pattern carries it", "a keyword the validator does not implement refuses the value; annotations and x- keys are ignored", "non-local refs and plain-name fragments are unresolvable", "implements the 2020-12 keywords it used to ignore", "the keyword lists are published", "is exact on the decimal values as written", "flags quantified groups whose body ends in a loose repetition, and not Zod's built-in patterns", "schemaProblems reports what the validator would refuse, with paths", "toJsonSchema marks every input node the server checks beyond JSON Schema with x-axe-refined", "the lint warns for each refined node, and the validator ignores the annotation", "the lint reports an unsupported construct in an action schema as an error", "the same key with a different date is conflict, even though both parse to a Date", "the fingerprint is the input as sent: a default filled in by the schema is a different request", "a login resume parses the input as sent once, so a transform does not run twice", "a payload schema whose pattern does not compile is invalid_input, not a crash".

`packages/generate/test/json-schema-to-zod.test.ts`: "never drops a constraint silently: length and pattern stay with a format, and what is dropped is named" (fails before); "falls back to unknown with a warning naming the path for what it does not handle" updated for the extra `not` warning.

### Limitations

- Zod refinements on `accepts[].schema` are still not applied on `/axe/continue` (the stored schema is JSON); `x-axe-refined` tells the agent, and the site checks in `onContinue`.
- The backtracking check is a heuristic (overlapping alternatives pass), and patterns run with no time limit.
- `$id` inside a schema does not change the base for `$ref`; refs resolve against the document root.
- `oneOf` from `@summationai/axe-generate` is converted as a union, so a value matching two alternatives is accepted there (the JSON validator enforces exactly one).
- Migration: a retry across the upgrade whose raw input differs from its parsed input (a stripped unknown member, a spelled-out default) gets `conflict` once. A hand-written JSON Schema that used an unsupported keyword, or a format with no checker and no pattern, now refuses every payload instead of ignoring it; `schemaProblems` or the lint finds these.

## Status

done

# docs/review/2026-09-24/13-execution-modes.md

# 13. Browser-local and server-side execution as explicit modes; reference app

Phase 3. Branch `review/reference-app`, based on `herz/surface-integration` at `7284f6a` (phases 1 and 2 merged).

## Finding

The review: a React hook registers closures in a browser; importing the same module in a Next route shares none of that registry, session, or state. The two modes had to be named, with a runnable React/Next reference application showing who owns each capability, with real handlers, authoritative server state, and tests for login, two actors, human changes between observe and act, navigation, reconnect, lost responses, and expired handoffs.

Checked in this checkout at `7284f6a`:

- Nothing in `spec/SURFACE.md` or `docs/` said where a surface runs. [S-DOM-2] called `expose` browser-local; `docs/surface.md` said "two tabs of one user still resolve as the application's state store resolves them today". Nothing said that a route handler importing `@summationai/axe-surface` gets another, empty surface, or that the SDK has no broker between a page and a server.
- A second registry inside one realm: `packages/surface/dist/react.js` inlined `src/index.ts`, including `createSurface` and the module-level `surface` (`grep -c "function createSurface" dist/react.js` was 1; `dist/react.js` imported only `react` and `@summationai/axe-core`). So `useSurface(entry, deps)` with the default target registered in a table that `surface.expose(window)` from `@summationai/axe-surface` never showed. The source tests could not see it: they import `src/`, where there is one module.
- The only runnable example, `docs/examples/demo/plan-board.ts`, is one Express process with one surface on the server; its page calls the AXE actions with a fixed bearer token. There was no browser-local capability, no session, no tenant, and no browser test.

## Change

Reference application, `examples/plan-review` (private workspace package `plan-review-example`; Next 16 App Router, React 19; `next` and `react` are its dependencies only; no `build` script, so it is outside `pnpm -r build`; its Node suite is in `pnpm -r test`):

- `lib/store.ts`: one plan per tenant with a revision column; `write(tenant, expectedRev, actor, event, mutate, operationId?)` is the conditional write (check and write with no `await` between them), records the history, and remembers applied operation ids. Sessions, members, agent tokens, and the app's index of approval requests. Instances live on globalThis, since Next evaluates modules per bundle layer.
- `lib/domain.ts`: the one implementation of every change (edit values, submit, lock, reopen, freeze), with one function (whyNot) that returns the sentence the page disables its button with, the AXE action's availability reason, and the refusal.
- `lib/axe.ts`: server capabilities. `createAXE` with `auth: { modes: ["user"] }` (agent bearer token or the page's session cookie), a per-tenant `tenant` resolver (anonymous callers see a public tenant with no plan data), `revision` = the plan's revision column, `requestPolicy: { trustedOrigins }`, and `onActionEvent` feeding approval events into the history. Actions `plan.read`, `plan.set-value`, `plan.submit`, `plan.approve` (item 15), `plan.history`; every write requires `expectedRev` and carries it into the conditional write; a stale one is `conflict` with `details: { expectedRev, currentRev }`.
- `lib/ui-api.ts`: the app's own endpoints (sign-in, state, values, submit, lock, reopen, freeze, approval decisions) under the same JSON and origin policy as the runtime, checked with isAcceptedOrigin and isJsonContentType from `@summationai/axe-core` whether or not a cookie is present.
- `lib/browser-surface.ts`: the browser-local surface, one per page instance, in `app` revision mode (the page adopts the plan's revision with `setRev`), ledger text hashed; exposePageSurface publishes it at `window.__surface`. This is the one module a WebMCP adapter (item 14) should hook.
- `app/plan/PlanBoard.tsx`: `useSurfaceProps` registrations on the page surface: a field per cell whose setter changes only the tab's unsaved draft, "Save N unsaved changes" (posts to the app's endpoint with the person's session and the revision the drafts were typed at, so a draft typed before someone else's save is refused rather than rebased by the page's polling), "Scroll to <month>", and "Open the approval requests". `app/history/page.tsx` is a second route for the navigation case; `app/approvals/[id]` is the approval page (item 15).
- Routes: `app/axe/[...axe]/route.ts` and `app/.well-known/axe.json/route.ts` with `axeNext`; `app/api/[...path]/route.ts` delegates to `lib/ui-api.ts`.
- Root scripts `example:dev`, `example:test`, `example:test:app`; `pnpm-workspace.yaml` includes `examples/*`; ESLint and Prettier ignore `.next` and Playwright output. Next's generated `next-env.d.ts` (which imports types from `.next/`) is ignored and `app-env.d.ts` carries its references, so the typecheck works on a fresh clone.

`@summationai/axe-surface` packaging (`packages/surface/tsup.config.ts`): an esbuild plugin makes the `/react` entry import `./index.js` (ESM) or `./index.cjs` (CommonJS) instead of inlining it, so the hooks' default target is the `surface` that `@summationai/axe-surface` exports. No source change; the browser bundle test is unchanged and passes.

Ownership and scoping:

| Capability | Where | Registered by | Reachable by | Scope | Lifetime |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| read plan, read history | server | `action()` | agents over AXE (HTTP, MCP) | caller's user and tenant | process |
| edit value, submit | server | `action()` → `lib/domain.ts` | agents over AXE; the page via `lib/ui-api.ts` | user, tenant; conditional write at the presented revision | process |
| ask to approve and lock | server | `action()` with `approvalState`, `onResume` | agents over AXE; decided on the app's page | user, tenant; approval bound to input, principal, tenant, revision | one hour, one use |
| approve or cancel a request, freeze, reopen, lock directly | server | the app's endpoints | a person with the session cookie, from the app's origin | the person's role in the tenant | process |
| draft a cell, Save, scroll, open the dialog | browser | `useSurfaceProps` on the page surface | code in the page (`window.__surface`) | this tab and page instance | while mounted |

Spec: `spec/SURFACE.md` v0.7, §9 "Execution modes": [S-MODE-1] (browser-local: one page instance, reachable only in that realm; the same module on a server is another, empty surface), [S-MODE-2] (server-side: process lifetime, runtime-scoped, never depends on a browser closure), [S-MODE-3] (no broker; an explicit connection only; shared state on the server behind a conditional write; `app` revision mode shares `expectedRev`), [S-MODE-4] (unmount unregisters, nothing on the server changes). Changes line and a v0.7 provenance paragraph.

Docs: new `docs/reference-app.md` (what it demonstrates, how to run the app and each suite, a five-step demo, the ownership table, a code tour included from the app's own typechecked source, the test list, supported behavior and deliberate limits, including "no browser-session broker"); `docs/surface.md` new section "Where a surface runs"; `docs/README.md` and `site/build.mjs` HUB_GROUPS; `docs/examples/demo/README.md` and `plan-board.ts` point at the reference app. `DECISIONS.md` ("Execution modes are a spec section", "The reference app is a workspace package outside the build graph"), `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Tests

Node suite, `examples/plan-review/test/server.test.ts`, in `pnpm -r test` (`pnpm example:test`): 15 passed. Item 13's cases:

- login: a session cookie per user and tenant; other origins and non-JSON posts are refused on both doors
- tenant scope: the same person on another team is another scope, for plans, tokens, and approvals
- two users editing the same plan: one conflict, one success, nothing lost silently (including two tabs saving at once)
- a person's change between the agent's observe and act is refused; the agent re-reads and continues
- a lost response is recovered by retrying with the same idempotency key; the edit applies once
- a new AXE client re-discovers the site and continues the approved request
- an MCP client reconnects on a new connection and resumes with `axe_resume`
- browser-local capabilities are never served over HTTP: the page's registry and the server's actions are separate
- the built `@summationai/axe-surface/react` uses `@summationai/axe-surface`'s registry instead of carrying a second one (fails with the previous `tsup.config.ts`: checked by stashing it and rebuilding)
- the expired-handoff case is under item 15

Browser suite, `examples/plan-review/e2e/plan-review.spec.ts`, Playwright 1.63 with Chromium against `next start` on port 3107 (`pnpm example:test:app`, which runs `next build` first): 7 passed. Item 13's cases:

- sign in, then an agent in the page drafts a value and saves it through the page's own Save (the manifest lists only the server actions)
- two people in two tabs edit the same cell: one save succeeds, the other is refused and keeps its draft
- a person changes the plan between the agent's observe and act: the agent is refused, re-reads, and continues
- navigation: the page's controls leave the surface on a route change; the server's plan is untouched

The browser run needs the Chromium build that `@playwright/test` 1.63 expects (`pnpm --filter plan-review-example exec playwright install chromium`); it was already installed here for the site's tests. `next dev` was also checked by hand: sign-in, the plan page, and the manifest answer.

## Limitations

- One process, in memory: plans, sessions, history, AXE tokens, and idempotency records reset on restart and are not shared between instances. The conditional write is the in-memory equivalent of `UPDATE ... WHERE rev = $expected`, not a database.
- Demo credentials: sign-in has no password; agent tokens are fixed strings.
- The page polls every 1.5 seconds; there is no push.
- The page surface is reachable only through `window.__surface`. Nothing here connects the page's controls to an agent outside the page, by design ([S-MODE-3]); a WebMCP adapter can hook `lib/browser-surface.ts`.
- The packaging fix gives one registry per module format. An application that loads `@summationai/axe-surface` as ESM and `@summationai/axe-surface/react` as CommonJS (unusual outside mixed toolchains) still gets two; the reference app passes its surface explicitly anyway, which is clearest.
- `spec/SURFACE.md` moves to v0.7 here; item 14 may also touch that file, so the version line may need reconciling at merge. `packages/surface/tsup.config.ts` may conflict with a new entry item 14 adds.

## Status

done

# docs/review/2026-09-24/14-agent-interface-adapters.md

# 14. Existing agent interfaces through adapters (WebMCP, elicitation, MCP Apps)

Phase 3. Branch `review/adapters`, based on `herz/surface-integration` at `7284f6a` (phases 1 and 2 merged).

## Finding

The review said AXE described itself as filling gaps that the agent ecosystem already fills in part, and that it should meet existing agent interfaces through adapters: WebMCP in the browser, MCP elicitation for requirements and handoffs, MCP Apps for presentation, and MCP's OAuth resource-server model for authorization.

Verified at `7284f6a`:

- `@summationai/axe-mcp` rendered every `needs_input` and `needs_human` as text and never used elicitation, even with a client that declared it. Its server declared only `tools`, so no MCP Apps view could exist.
- `docs/mcp.md` "What does not map" already named elicitation and MCP Apps as counterparts "this bridge does not use yet" (item 10 changed it), but `docs/faq.md` said MCP gives a site no escalation ladder, no `display` hints, and no human-handoff semantics, and mentioned neither elicitation, Apps, nor MCP's OAuth model. The FAQ's OAuth answer did not separate verifying tokens (which `@summationai/axe-mcp` does since item 9) from issuing them (which nothing in the SDK does).
- A Surface could be reached by a browser agent only through `expose(window)` or the DOM; there was no WebMCP path. The `@summationai/axe-surface` plus `/react` browser bundle was 31,370 bytes minified.
- `docs/why-axe.md`, `docs/for-agent-builders.md`, and `README.md` made no incorrect claim about MCP; they did not mention these MCP features either.

## Change

### WebMCP: `@summationai/axe-surface/webmcp`

`packages/surface/src/webmcp.ts` (new subpath export; `tsup.config.ts`, `package.json` `exports` and typesVersions, `typedoc.json`):

- `exposeWebMcp(surface, options)`: finds `document.modelContext` with `registerTool` (or `options.modelContext`; `null` disables). Absent: registers nothing and returns `{ supported: false, reason }`. Present: registers `surface_observe` (read-only, `untrustedContentHint`) and one tool per action, non-sensitive field, and collection with `more`. Descriptions come from `describeEntry`, plus what the tool does and, when unavailable, the handoff or the kinds that would unblock it. Input schema `{ expectedRev?, text? (the field's schema and maxLength), confirm? }` with `additionalProperties: false`. `consequentialHint` on a control that is not reversible.
- Follows `subscribe`, diffs by name, description, schema, and annotations, and re-registers only what changed (abort the old signal, register again). Rounds are serialized, since the draft rejects a duplicate name. `unavailable: "describe" | "omit"`.
- `execute` calls `surface.act` with the call's `expectedRev`, or the surface's current revision when omitted; `actor` defaults to `webmcp`; `run` is forwarded. Result: `{ content: [text], structuredContent: envelope, isError? }`.
- `webMcpToolNames(ids, prefix)`: letters, digits, `_`, `-`; an FNV-1a hash of the id on a collision or on the observe tool's name; at most 128 characters.
- The browser API is reached only in resolveModelContext and registerOne.

Spec: `spec/SURFACE.md` v0.7, §8 "WebMCP: the browser's own agent", [S-WEB-1] to [S-WEB-5]; provenance line.

### Elicitation in `@summationai/axe-mcp`

`packages/mcp/src/elicitation.ts` (new) and `packages/mcp/src/index.ts` (`finish`, offerPage, and an `Interaction` built in the CallTool handler):

- `elicitationModes(capabilities)`: `{}` means form only (the specification's backwards-compatibility rule).
- `isSensitiveAccept`: `sensitive: true`, `payment.*`, `identity.*`, `credential(s).*`, and kind names containing password, passcode, secret, token, api-key, private-key, OTP, or PIN.
- `toFormSchema`: the MCP form subset (flat object of string, number, integer, boolean, single- and multi-select enum; string formats email, uri, date, date-time). Nested objects, unions, and references return null; a primitive schema is wrapped as `value`.
- planElicitation: walk `accepts` in order; the first non-sensitive kind with a form rendering gets a form; a sensitive kind met first gets URL mode if the client declared it and the `fallback` URL is https (or loopback http), else nothing.
- Form `accept`: `/axe/continue` with the token, the kind, the answer, and the call's `expectedRev`, as the same caller; a `pending` continuation is polled within the budget; up to three forms per tool call. `decline`, `cancel`, or an error: the original result with a note.
- `needs_human` with URL mode: the handoff URL is offered, except for `login_required`. `accept` is reported as consent to open, and the resume token stays in the text.
- The request is sent with relatedRequestId (on the tool call's own response stream over HTTP), the call's abort signal, and `timeout` (option `elicitation.timeoutMs`, default 600000). `elicitation: false` turns it off.

Spec: §22 [P-MCP-6] (form mode), [P-MCP-7] (sensitive kinds, URL mode, `login_required`, the handoff page identifies the user). Mapped in `packages/testing/src/conformance/requirements.ts`.

### MCP Apps view in `@summationai/axe-mcp` (experimental)

`packages/mcp/src/apps.ts` (new): the extension id, the MIME type, `ui://axe/presentation`, and the view's HTML. In `index.ts` the server declares `resources: {}` unless `apps: false`. `tools/list` adds `_meta.ui.resourceUri` to `display` tools, `resources/list` lists the view, and `ok` results carry `_meta["axe/presentation"].html` (from `toHTML`), all only when `capabilities.extensions["io.modelcontextprotocol/ui"].mimeTypes` includes `text/html;profile=mcp-app`. `resources/read` serves the view with `_meta.ui.prefersBorder`. `formatResult(result, action, brand, { presentation })`.

The view: inline style and script only; sends `ui/initialize` (protocol version `2026-01-26`) and `ui/notifications/initialized`, renders on `ui/notifications/tool-result`; accepts messages only from `window.parent`; parses the HTML with `DOMParser`; removes `script`, `iframe`, `object`, `embed`, `form`, `link`, `meta`, `base`, the affordance buttons, every `on*` and `srcdoc` attribute, and non-http(s) `href` and `src`; falls back to the text content in a `<pre>`; routes link clicks through `ui/open-link` when the host offers openLinks.

Spec: §22 [P-MCP-8].

### Docs, vocabulary, and the rest

- `docs/webmcp.md` (new; `docs/README.md` item 15; `site/build.mjs` "Reference" group); example `docs/examples/webmcp/page.ts`.
- `docs/mcp.md`: mapping rows for `ok`, `needs_input`, `needs_human`; "What maps to MCP's own features, and what does not" replaces "What does not map"; new sections "Elicitation" and "MCP Apps view (experimental)"; example `docs/examples/mcp/elicitation.ts`.
- `docs/surface.md`: a paragraph pointing to WebMCP after `expose`.
- `spec/VOCABULARY.md` "Agent interface adapters": `exposeWebMcp`, `modelContext`, `registerTool`, `consequentialHint`, `requestedSchema`; `packages/core/src/vocabulary.ts` regenerated.
- `CHANGELOG.md`, `DECISIONS.md` ("Existing agent interfaces"), `.changeset/agent-interface-adapters.md`, API reference regenerated.

### Docs corrections

| File | Old claim | New text |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `docs/faq.md`, "How is this different from MCP?" | MCP alone does not give a site "an escalation ladder (a tool either returns or errors), `display` hints, and human handoff semantics". | MCP has elicitation (form and URL modes), the Apps extension, and OAuth resource-server authorization, and the derived server uses them; WebMCP plays that role in the browser. AXE adds discovery at a domain, typed kinds with shared shapes and sensitivity, a three-rung ladder whose follow-ups resume with tokens bound to caller and tenant, revision-guarded live state, and honesty rules with an audit. |
| `docs/faq.md`, "What about authentication and OAuth?" | "No OAuth 2.1 authorization server ships in v0." (nothing on the resource-server side) | Kept and marked deliberate; added that `@summationai/axe-mcp` is a resource server (verifies each token, publishes RFC 9728 metadata) and issuing tokens stays with the site's authorization server. |
| `docs/mcp.md`, "What does not map" | Handoff and presentation had no counterpart the bridge used ("this bridge does not use it yet"); "The derived server declares only tools in v0." | Three lists: what maps to MCP's own features (elicitation, Apps, OAuth resource server; issuing tokens deliberately out of scope), what AXE adds, and what has no counterpart (discovery, idempotency keys, prompts and sampling, streaming). |
| `docs/why-axe.md`, "An MCP server for free" | (no MCP comparison) | Adds that the derived server uses elicitation and the Apps extension with clients that support them. |
| `docs/for-agent-builders.md`, opening | (no MCP comparison) | One sentence: the derived server uses elicitation and Apps when the client declares them. |

`README.md` makes no claim that MCP lacks these features and is unchanged. `llms.txt` is left to the coordinator.

## Tests

`packages/surface/test/webmcp.test.ts` (jsdom; a fake `document.modelContext` enforcing the draft's `registerTool` checks: name characters and length, duplicate name, empty description; abort unregisters; results serialized to JSON as the draft specifies):

- without WebMCP: registers nothing, says so, and leaves the page and expose() working (absent API, an object without `registerTool`, `modelContext: null`)
- registers an observe tool and one tool per control, with describeEntry text and JSON input schemas; a sensitive field is never exposed
- acts through the page's own surface at the latest revision, passes expectedRev, and maps the result to text and structured content
- follows availability: a changed reason re-registers the tool, `omit` drops an unavailable control, and a freeze is described
- maps ids to valid, stable, unique tool names and reports a refused registration

`packages/surface/test/bundle.test.ts`: the `@summationai/axe-surface` plus `/react` bundle contains no `webmcp` input (new assertion); `@summationai/axe-surface/webmcp` bundles alone for the browser without Zod or React (new test; 34,627 bytes alone, since it includes the main entry; about 5.6 kB on top of `@summationai/axe-surface`).

`packages/mcp/test/elicitation.test.ts` (the SDK `Client`, with and without the capability):

- in memory: a client without the capability gets the needs_input text as before; a form-capable client is asked for a non-sensitive kind in a flat form, and the answer continues the action; decline and cancel return the needs_input result to the model, whose axe_continue still works; a sensitive kind is never put in a form, URL mode offers the site's page when the client has it, otherwise the text (form-only and form+URL clients); needs_human is offered as the site's page in URL mode, never in a form, login_required is left to MCP authorization; `elicitation: false` keeps every result as text; only schemas in the form subset become forms, sensitivity is decided before the schema
- over real HTTP (`serveHttp` behind `node:http` on 127.0.0.1, SDK `StreamableHTTPClientTransport`, the OAuth verifier and `clientFor`): over HTTP sessions the form reaches the calling client mid-call, and the continuation runs as that caller (a second user without the capability gets text; the site records `create:alice`, `continue:alice`, `create:bob`); over HTTP sessions a URL-capable client is offered the handoff page; stateless HTTP cannot carry a server request, so the client gets the text

`packages/mcp/test/apps.test.ts`: a host that negotiated the extension gets the ui:// view on display tools and the escaped rendering with each result (an injected `<img onerror>` and `<script>` come out escaped; the view has no external script, link, frame, or URL); a host without the extension sees no view, no resource, and the same text result (also a host declaring another MIME type, and `apps: false`); over HTTP sessions the view is negotiated per session.

`packages/mcp/test/apps-view.test.ts` (jsdom, a stand-in host in the parent window speaking the extension's messages): the view initializes with the host, renders the escaped presentation, and runs nothing from the result; without a presentation in the result, the view shows the text content.

Restoring `packages/mcp/src/index.ts` to `7284f6a` removes exports the new test files import, so they fail to load. With the code in place but both features off by default (checked by flipping the two defaults), nine of the thirteen elicitation and Apps tests fail; the four that pass are "a client without the capability", "`elicitation: false`", the stateless-HTTP test, and the schema unit test, which pin the fallback. The existing `mcp.test.ts`, `http.test.ts`, and `freshness.test.ts` pass unchanged; their clients declare neither capability.

## Limitations

- WebMCP is a draft behind a flag and an origin trial in one browser (Chrome 149 and later, as of September 2026). The adapter was tested against a fake that implements the documented shape, not in Chrome. If the draft changes, resolveModelContext and registerOne change. Earlier builds with `navigator.modelContext` are not detected.
- The WebMCP adapter offers no ledger tool and no way to supply a `requires` kind to an unavailable control; the AXE bridge's `/axe/continue` does that server-side.
- Elicitation needs a connection that can carry a server request during the call. Stateless HTTP cannot, so its clients always get text.
- URL-mode elicitation does not wait for the user, and the bridge sends no `notifications/elicitation/complete`, since it cannot observe completion on the site. The model still calls `axe_resume`.
- One form per `needs_input`, for the first suitable kind. A site whose preferred kind is sensitive gets URL mode or text even when a later kind would fit a form. Dropped keywords (formats outside the four) are checked by the site on continue, so a user can submit a value the site refuses with `invalid_input`.
- The sensitivity rule is a floor over the site's flag plus a name heuristic; a custom sensitive kind with an innocuous name must be marked `sensitive: true`, as [K-4] already requires.
- The Apps view is experimental and was tested under jsdom with a stand-in host, not in a shipping host. It shows no images (the host's default CSP allows none from other origins and the view declares no resourceDomains), and it hides the affordance buttons rather than wiring them to `tools/call`. The server announces the `resources` capability to every client.
- MCP authorization-server operation (issuing tokens) is not provided, deliberately; `@summationai/axe-mcp` remains a resource server (item 9).

## Sources verified

All read on 2026-09-24 with a web fetch. Claims in code and docs rest on these unless listed as unverified.

- WebMCP specification, W3C Web Machine Learning Community Group, Draft Community Group Report of 17 September 2026, <https://webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp/>: `ModelContext` on `Document` (`document.modelContext`), `[SecureContext]`; `registerTool(tool, { signal, exposedTo })` returns a promise resolved after registration; rejects with `InvalidStateError` for an empty name, a name over 128 characters or with characters other than ASCII alphanumerics, `_`, `-`, `.`, a duplicate name, or an empty description; aborting the signal unregisters; getTools, executeTool; `toolchange`, `toolactivated`, `toolcancel` events; the `execute(input, { signal })` result is serialized to a JSON string; annotations `readOnlyHint`, `untrustedContentHint`, `consequentialHint`, `debugging`. No `navigator.modelContext`, provideContext, unregisterTool, or clearContext.
- WebMCP explainer, <https://github.com/webmachinelearning/webmcp>: the same `document.modelContext` shape; an example `execute` returning `{ content: [{ type: "text", text }] }`.
- Chrome, "WebMCP", <https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/webmcp>, last updated 7 August 2026: origin trial from Chrome 149, flag `chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing`, "under active discussion and subject to change". Chrome, imperative API page, <https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/webmcp/imperative-api>, last updated 21 September 2026: `document.modelContext.registerTool`, feature detection with `document.modelContext?.registerTool`.
- MCP specification 2025-11-25, "Elicitation", <https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/client/elicitation>: capability `elicitation: { form, url }`, `{}` equals form only, servers must not send undeclared modes; form `requestedSchema` limited to flat primitive properties (formats email, uri, date, date-time; enums with and without titles; multi-select arrays); servers must not use form mode for passwords, API keys, access tokens, or payment credentials and must use URL mode for them; URL mode carries elicitationId and `url`, and `accept` is consent, not completion; `notifications/elicitation/complete` is optional; the URL must not be pre-authenticated or carry sensitive user data; the server must verify that the user who opens the URL is the user who started the elicitation; URL mode must not be used to authorize the user to the MCP server itself.
- MCP specification 2025-11-25, "Authorization", <https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/authorization>: an MCP server is an OAuth 2.1 resource server and the authorization server may be separate; servers must implement RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, validate token audience, answer 401 and 403 with `WWW-Authenticate`, and must not pass tokens through; authorization is optional, and stdio servers should take credentials from the environment.
- MCP Apps overview, <https://apps.extensions.modelcontextprotocol.io/api/documents/overview.html>, and specification SEP-1865 "MCP Apps", status Stable, version 2026-01-26, <https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps> (`specification/2026-01-26/apps.mdx`): extension id `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui`; the host declares `capabilities.extensions[...]` with `mimeTypes: ["text/html;profile=mcp-app"]`; servers SHOULD check it before registering UI tools and declare nothing themselves; resources are `ui://…` with that MIME type, served by `resources/read` as `text`, and may be left out of `resources/list`; tools use `_meta.ui.resourceUri` (the flat `ui/resourceUri` is deprecated); `_meta.ui.prefersBorder` and `_meta.ui.csp`; view messages `ui/initialize` (protocol version `2026-01-26`), `ui/notifications/initialized`, `ui/notifications/tool-input`, `ui/notifications/tool-result` carrying a `CallToolResult`; `ui/open-link` needs the host's openLinks; default CSP `default-src 'none'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; media-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'none'`; hosts without Apps treat the tool as text-only.
- Installed `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.30.1 (read in `node_modules`): `Server.elicitInput(params, options)` checks `elicitation.form` and `url` and validates form answers against `requestedSchema`; `ElicitRequestFormParamsSchema`, `ElicitRequestURLParamsSchema` (`url` must parse as a URL); the client-capabilities schema normalizes `elicitation: {}` to `{ form: {} }`; `ClientCapabilities.extensions` is a free record. No types or helpers for MCP Apps.

Unverified: the WebMCP adapter in Chrome itself (no browser run); the Apps view in a shipping host (only jsdom with a stand-in host); that hosts pass the tool result's `_meta` to the view unchanged (the specification says the notification's params are the `CallToolResult`, which includes `_meta`).
